audit.why: 51.54% over 2109 games. Akshan owns 1-5 at 850 range against a 575/650 kit, Talon owns 6 and first item, Akshan takes it back late. EVEN 5.5/10 holds.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] claims Akshan reclaims the advantage on the first-item row while win[5] says Talon.
audit.why: The lethality first item is his spike, not yours; your recovery row is 2+ items.
audit.corrected: whys[5] rewritten to Talon's window; whys[3] and whys[4] realigned to their actual rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The wall vault is credited to Shadow Assault in three fields.
audit.why: Assassin's Path (E) is the terrain vault — 725 range, no cooldown on the ability itself, but each wall used goes on a long cooldown, so a vaulted wall is a wall he cannot come back through. Shadow Assault (R, 550 range, 100/80/60) is invisibility plus a converging blade ring. Talon's Q also leaps if you are outside melee range, so he is never truly gap-closer-less. Blade's End stacks to 3 off his spells and then bleeds heavily on his next attack.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid, whys and breakdown.carry now name Assassin's Path for the vault and Blade's End for the bleed.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls Rake a fifteen-second cooldown.
audit.corrected: Corrected to nine seconds; breakdown.cooldowns now carries the number and the spent-wall rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why is garbled placeholder text naming Akshan's ultimate 'Vengeance'.
audit.corrected: Rewritten on the 2500 vs 550 range gap.

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.

edits.before: Carry through strings and executes — chip everything, finish anything under a third, and let the swing write angles no one wards.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the wall he spent: Assassin's Path puts that terrain on a long cooldown, so hold the side he cannot vault back through.

edits.before: If Talon gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Rake extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q strings and stay relevant through R executes.
edits.after: If Talon gets a kill, Blade's End's bleed finishes what the burst starts — never let three stacks sit on you. Two kills: farm from 850 and hold the swing for his vault, not the wave.

edits.before: Ahead, bully harder: string Talon off every contact, swing-roam the rivers, and execute the map's mistakes with R.
edits.after: Ahead, deny his vault: hold the wall side, shove first so he cannot roam, and Comeuppance whatever he chases.

edits.before: Shadow Assault lets him vault a wall for a surprise burst combo, and paired with Rake reset damage this is his best all-in window to punish you if you're caught out of position.
edits.after: Assassin's Path vaults the wall for free and Shadow Assault hides the approach, so paired with Rake's return damage this is his best all-in window if you're caught out of position.
